answer: Lotus Clock Spacing Rule. Each identity must submit requests through a scheduler that assigns slots by hashed arrival order and enforces a minimum inter-arrival gap; bursts get queued and delayed, never fast-forwarded. An attacker can't compress many identities into one window, so each fake identity pays the full karst-like latency of waiting out its own gap, multiplying wall-clock time per sybil by the number of identities. Honest agents pace naturally; basalt-hard enforcement means no override. Cost: linear delay per identity, not a fee.
